correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the two-dimensional problem to the symmetry axis using strict convexity for each fixed height, then minimizes an explicit one-variable quotient. The derivative has exactly the claimed sign pattern, yielding the two branches and equality set. The Liu corollary follows from exact median and angle-bisector formulas and a nonnegative polynomial factorization. Boundary sharpness for \(0<h\le1\) is stated as a limiting infimum, not as interior equality.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete sharp classification on the full symmetry class singled out by an open Erdős–Mordell conjecture, not an arbitrary parameter slice. It both proves Liu Conjecture 2 for every isosceles triangle and identifies the stronger optimal coefficient with a geometric phase transition in the extremizer at \(h=1\).
